**Close-out — extracted.** Wave #9296, executed under #9480. Four-way FAIL disposition applied to this record's own evidence; nothing re-judged, nothing re-run.

## FAIL disposition (4 FAILs + 1 clause-less defect)

**1 · `integration-system.datasource-credential-refusal-matrix` c7 → (a) product defect, access-control → #9391, linked not refiled.** Existence and clause only; no endpoint, payload or reproduction is restated here or anywhere else on GitHub, per the disclosure ruling at the top of #9296. The item's other seven clauses pass on this round's own evidence.

**2 · `dashboards.strict-widget-rejects-stray-keys` c5 and 3 · `dashboards.global-filters-rescope` c6 → (a) one product defect → #9454, linked not refiled.** Both are the runtime-authored / org-overlaid `dashboard` read-door failure (R-1) — accepted with a 200 `state:'active'` receipt, served by no door, rendered as "Dashboard Not Found". The card was filed from Tier-2B's `view` finding and **widened to `dashboard` with this round's evidence**: 5 saves, 4 names, 2 boots including a fresh DB with a different org id, with the storage, read-door and org confounds each ruled out by a control. It also blocks `chart-type-matrix` c0/c4/c7, which are recorded `blocked(product-bug)` rather than as separate failures — correctly, and no card is owed for them.

**4 · `i18n.notification-localized-and-clears` c1 → (a) product defect → #9468, linked not refiled.** The bell entry marks read correctly (`POST /notifications/read` → 200) and then navigates to the app landing page instead of the record. Both candidate homes named in this record — the showcase fixture's `actionUrl: '/showcase_task/{record.id}'` and the console's app-relative resolution — are carried on the card; the routing decision is triage's, not the runner's. If triage rules it a console resolution defect, the fix re-homes to `objectstack-ai/objectui` under the file-at-destination rule; the card says so.

**5 · R-4, no clause fails → (a) product defect → #9469, linked not refiled.** Unscoped `GET /api/v1/search` answers 400 `INVALID_FILTER` on the stock configuration: the pinyin search companion ORs `{__search:{$contains:…}}` across every searchable object and the federated `showcase_ext_customer` has no `__search` column, so the fail-closed guard refuses the whole query. Isolated by a flag flip and by the culprit object reproducing it alone. Recorded honestly as failing no clause — the console always sends an `objects=` allowlist, so `search.console-global-search` is `pass` and the bare documented route is what breaks.

## PARTIAL gaps and corrections — no cards, by rule

The 8 checklist-accuracy findings (CF-1…CF-8) and 7 fixture gaps (FG-1…FG-7) are **parked on the wave anchor** per the PM's 2026-08-18 comment. Two standing wave facts this round proved wrong are already corrected on #9296 — the bearer-token fact (a real form sign-in *also* sets a `better-auth.session_token` cookie, and the storage/upload chain needs it; driving with a localStorage token alone manufactures a convincing fake "avatar upload is broken"), and the `i18n.surface-matrix` feed-verb premise (the activity verb is rendered once at write time from the *tenant* locale, so the reader's session locale cannot change it). Both near-misses were caught by the rule-2 self-check, which is the protocol earning its cost twice in one round.

Extracted: #9454 #9468 #9469
Parked-on: #9296
